The 35-economy figure belongs to the separate Joint Statement on AI Opportunity. An overstatement of roughly 25%, uncorrected.
- [FALSE] (scope) Pax Silica is "23-member strong" — claimed by President Marcos · State of the Nation Address, 27 Jul 2026. Stated in the annual address to Congress. The State Department count that day was 24. The figure is not random: on that date the State Department’s own Pax Silica page listed 23 signatories and omitted the United States from its own roster, so counting the page yielded 23. Two outlets repeated it within the week. CORRECTION, 21 Aug 2026 — this note previously described the page in the present tense. Checked directly on 21 August 2026 the page lists 24 signatories, Italy now among them, and still omits the United States, so counting it now yields 24 against a standing count of 25. The roster defect this note identifies survives the update. The same government produced an overstatement of roughly 25% and an understatement of one within four days, neither corrected publicly.
- [PROJECTION] (legal & social) BCDA targets signing of the framework agreement by November 2026, potentially during the ASEAN Summit — claimed by BCDA. Finance Sec. Go, 7 July 2026: "I hope we can get something signed within the year" — Manila Bulletin reports the remark as referring to the framework agreement for the hub, with Foxconn described separately as a possible anchor locator; no transcript was located, so the scope rests on the outlet’s framing. On 19 August 2026 BusinessWorld and GMA News reported BCDA president Joshua M. Bingcang saying BCDA was still aiming for November but that negotiations could take longer, rendering his description of the target as "not set in stone" (BusinessWorld) and "not cast in stone" (GMA News). Those are the same remarks by the same official on the same day and are not independent corroboration; the two outlets name the forum differently and this report asserts no venue, and no transcript or recording was located to resolve the wording. Correction (v2.32): this note previously read "Other statements point to 2027 finalisation". That was mis-scoped — the Presidential Communications Office release of 23 July 2026 places planning in 2027, with contract negotiations expected during 2026 and construction expected to begin in early 2028, not framework finalisation. The sequence is retained in the timeline and withdrawn from here. The verdict is an official target that the proponent has publicly described as subject to negotiation and possible delay. On 14–15 September, several outlets carrying remarks from the same press encounter with Trade Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo reported continued government optimism about a November signature, subject to continuing consultation and safeguards. These reports are not independent corroboration, no primary transcript was located, and they do not convert the target into a confirmed signing date.
- [VERIFIED] (legal & social) The USTR imposed a 12.5% forced-labour tariff on Philippine exports — claimed by Office of the US Trade Representative. Published 23 July and effective 24 July 2026, finding the Philippines "has failed to impose and effectively enforce a forced-labor import prohibition." Verified against the Federal Register notice, the measure carries exemptions, semiconductors and other Section 232-covered articles, donations, informational materials, and an excluded-products annex expanded by 471 HTS subheadings, and it replaced a Section 122 surcharge of 10%, documented to Federal Register doc. 2026-03824, which expired at the same minute the new action began. For goods covered by both, the net increment is roughly +2.5 percentage points. For the exempt goods, which include semiconductors, coconuts, pineapples, bananas and nickel ores, the change was a decrease of about 10 points. The signal stands even as the magnitude shrinks.

Official texts, published documents, statutes, statistical releases and FOI responses. Treated as evidence of what was said or recorded, not of whether it is true.

- T1-27 (3 Sep 2026): Fact Sheet — Trump Administration Launches Foundry School to Build the Workforce Behind America’s Manufacturing Comeback — US Department of State, Office of the Spokesperson — Added v2.46. The launch of Foundry School, described by the Department as a flagship initiative of Pax Silica: seventeen sessions across eight US universities, seven regional sessions from September 2026 and a ten-session Stanford core programme from January 2027, each taught by founders and chief executives from advanced manufacturing enterprises. It supplies a programme structure and start months, which is why section 12.4 withdraws two words it had carried since an early version. It supplies no cost, no individual session dates and no training-place allocation. It names the Republic of Korea, Japan, Taiwan and India among Pax Silica participants; the Philippines is not named, and the wording is illustrative rather than an eligibility list, so no inference of exclusion is drawn. Its figure of 3.8 million is a projection of United States manufacturing positions needing to be filled by 2033, not a Foundry School output target. This page superseded, at the same URL, the media advisory read on 2 September that the news-rail gate refused as prospective. — www.state.gov
- T1-28 (4 Sep 2026): BCDA, NCIP update community census in Capas, Tarlac for proposed Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park — Bases Conversion and Development Authority — Added v2.46. The proponent agency’s own account of the updated community census at Sitio Sapang Kawayan, led by NCIP Secretary Nancy A. Catamco and BCDA officer-in-charge senior vice president Mark P. Torres. It is the first BCDA-owned publication located using the name Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park, and it calls the park proposed throughout. It publishes no enumeration result: BCDA told reporters the same day that the exercise is an update and validation of the existing community census rather than a new enumeration, and that final figures are still being consolidated with the NCIP. Nothing in it identifies the activity as a Section 59 field-based investigation, a Certification Precondition process or an FPIC proceeding. — bcda.gov.ph

- T1-48 (24 Jun 2019): ECC-OL-R03-2019-0304, New Clark City Land Development Project — DENR-EMB Region III, as published by BCDA in its National Academy of Sports bidding documents — Environmental Compliance Certificate, read in full including Annex A. - T1-49 (Issue date not recorded in this register): EMB Memorandum Circular 2014-005, coverage-screening and threshold guidelines — DENR Environmental Management Bureau — Page 26 defines items 3.6.5 and 3.6.6, the industrial-park thresholds relevant to the 2019 certificate (T1-48). — eia.emb.gov.ph
- T1-50 (Published 28 Jul 2026; duties applicable from 12:01 a.m. EDT, 24 Jul 2026): Notice of Actions in Section 301 Investigations of Acts, Policies, and Practices of Various Economies Related to the Failure of Each Economy To Impose and Effectively Enforce a Prohibition on the Importation of Goods Produced With Forced Labor — Office of the United States Trade Representative, Federal Register document 2026-15181 — Operative notice, retrieved 13 Sep 2026. Imposes 12.5 percent tariffs on products of the Philippines, except as provided in Annex I and Annex II, Part A; articles subject to Section 232 tariffs are among the exemptions. The action followed the President’s direction of 23 July 2026. — www.federalregister.gov
- T1-51 (25 Nov 2025): Average Monthly Wage Rate of Time-Rated Workers on Full-Time Basis in the Philippines was at PhP 21,544 in 2024 — Philippine Statistics Authority, 2024 Occupational Wages Survey, Reference No. 2025-425 — Official statistics release, retrieved 13 Sep 2026 through a browser session because the site sits behind an anti-bot challenge. Reports the 2024 average monthly wage rate of time-rated workers on full-time basis at PHP 21,544 (basic pay PHP 20,309 plus allowances PHP 1,235). The survey covers formal establishments employing 10 or more workers only, so it benchmarks formal-sector pay generally, not semiconductor pay; the annual PHP 258,528 is this register’s ×12 arithmetic, not a PSA figure. — psa.gov.ph
- T1-52 (8 Nov 2024): Republic Act No. 12066, amending the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997 (CREATE MORE) — Congress of the Philippines; text as published by The Lawphil Project, Arellano Law Foundation — Statute text, retrieved 13 Sep 2026. Dated November 08, 2024, with the signature block “Approved: NOV 08 2024”; the popular name CREATE MORE does not appear in the retrieved title. Confirms the 5% SCIT on gross income for export enterprises, the enhanced deductions regime including a “One hundred percent (100%) additional deduction on power expense”, a 20% rate for enterprises under that regime, and incentive periods of up to 14–17 or 24–27 years depending on location and industry priorities. A legal-database copy, not the Official Gazette, which refused automated retrieval; it contains no estimate of incentive cost. — lawphil.net
- T1-53 (3 Sep 2025): Republic Act No. 12252, An Act Liberalizing the Lease of Private Lands by Foreign Investors, amending Republic Act No. 7652 (Investors’ Lease Act) — Congress of the Philippines; text as published by The Lawphil Project, Arellano Law Foundation — Statute text, retrieved 13 Sep 2026; signature block “Approved: SEP 03 2025”. Confirms that the aggregate period of the lease contract “shall not exceed ninety-nine (99) years”, that the President may impose a shorter period on the recommendation of the FIRB or other agencies, and that the Act concerns the lease of private lands. Says nothing about this project or about land administered by BCDA. A legal-database copy, not the Official Gazette. — lawphil.net
- T1-54 (29 Oct 1997): Republic Act No. 8371, The Indigenous Peoples Rights Act of 1997 — Congress of the Philippines (Tenth Congress); text as published by The Lawphil Project, Arellano Law Foundation — Statute text, retrieved 13 Sep 2026. Confirms the definitions of native title and of free and prior informed consent, the recognition of ancestral domain rights “by virtue of Native Title” with a CADT as formal recognition “when solicited” (§11), the rule that no community will be relocated without its free and prior informed consent, and the §59 certification precondition before any concession, license or lease is granted. Establishes the legal standard only, not whether any ancestral domain overlaps the parcel. A legal-database copy, not the Official Gazette. — lawphil.net
- T1-55 (11 Jun 1978): Presidential Decree No. 1586, Establishing an Environmental Impact Statement System, including other environmental management related measures — Office of the President; text as published by The Lawphil Project, Arellano Law Foundation — Decree text, retrieved 13 Sep 2026; “DONE in the City of Manila, this 11th day of June … nineteen hundred and seventy-eight.” Section 4 bars undertaking or operating a declared environmentally critical project or area without first securing an Environmental Compliance Certificate. Which projects are covered is set by later issuances (T1-56, T1-49), not by the decree itself. A legal-database copy, not the Official Gazette. — lawphil.net
- T1-56 (Issue date not shown in the retrieved copy): DENR Administrative Order No. 2003-30, Implementing Rules and Regulations for the Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System — Department of Environment and Natural Resources; copy hosted by Osaka University’s GreenAccess repository — Full text of the order, retrieved 13 Sep 2026; EMB’s own copy at eia.emb.gov.ph returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. §4.1: “only projects that pose potential significant impact to the environment shall be required to secure ECC’s”; §4.3 defines Categories A–D; §4.4 requires an ECC for Category A and B projects, with programmatic or locator-specific ECCs for ecozones; §4.6 lets Category D projects secure a Certificate of Non-Coverage. A third-party scan with minor OCR errors, not a DENR-certified copy. — greenaccess.law.osaka-u.ac.jp

Cited as an illustration of an information vacuum being filled by unofficial actors, not as a source of fact. — paxsilicaph.org — referenced but not obtained by this assessment — 12 documents referenced but not obtained by this assessment — These are cited by the parties or required by the analysis but were not obtained in the documented searches; absence here does not prove non-publication or nonexistence. They are listed so a reader can see exactly where the evidence stops. — A-01 — BCDA, DFA, US State Dept — Annex A, maps of the proposed 4,000-acre site — Defines the parcel. Every environmental, social, valuation and displacement question depends on it. — A-02 — BCDA — Supplemental Agreement on boundaries, legal description and operating terms — Would fix location, term and rent; no executed version located in the reviewed public record. — A-03 — BCDA, DTI, US State Dept — Framework agreement, the draft arrangement in exchange since 16 Jul 2026 or earlier — The operative instrument, target signature November 2026. — A-04 — BCDA — The scientific studies behind the US$40 to 70bn, jobs, tax and export figures — The entire economic case rests on these. — A-05 — BCDA — Water balance and impounding dam design — The binding physical constraint. — A-06 — BCDA, DOE, NGCP — Grid interconnection and adequacy study — The second binding constraint. — A-07 — DOF, BOI, PEZA — Tax-expenditure estimate for the incentive package — The missing half of the fiscal ledger. — A-08 — US DFC — DFC feasibility study, LNG terminal and at least 1,200 MW plant — Feasibility-study record, not a committed generation plan. — A-10 — Dow Jones — Wall Street Journal report on US jurisdiction — The origin of the immunity dispute. — A-11 — NCIP — NCIP records on Aeta CADT applications over Capas, 1999, 2014 and May 2019 — Determines FPIC obligations. — A-12 — DENR-EMB Region III — Underlying EIS and current-validity determination for the obtained 2019 New Clark City land-development ECC — The certificate, not the missing underlying EIS or current-validity determination named above, was obtained from BCDA’s published bidding documents and corrected two things. Correction (v2.38): this entry previously dated the certificate to 2017 and called it a master-plan ECC; it is dated 24 June 2019 and is issued for the "proposed New Clark City Land Development Project", 9,450.00 hectares under four TCTs. Correction (v2.38): EMB classified it under MC 2014-005 item 3.6.5, "Industrial Parks (horizontal development) with critical slopes", and issued it after an EIS was submitted — so the earlier statement that no EIS-backed zone-level ECC existed is withdrawn. What survives on its face: no manufacturing, semiconductor, data-centre or mineral-processing component is enumerated; Restriction 25 subjects any expansion or modification of approved components to new EIA requirements and requires individual locator ECCs; and it states that it does not create any right nor be used as an authorization to implement the project. It predates Pax Silica and so could not have assessed it as the project now announced. Whether the Pax Silica parcel lies within its boundary is not established, in either direction; its current validity was not determined. Still not obtained: the underlying EIS. BCDA said on 23 July 2026 that the DENR assessment need not conclude before the November signing. — A-13 — Office of the President, NEDA — Cabinet and NEDA Board records on the Philippine position — Whether the Republic formally deliberated. — What we deliberately did not count as evidence: search-result pages, AI-written summaries, sites that republish without naming a source, and press releases reprinted elsewhere and then counted as independent confirmation. Wikipedia was used only to cross-check dates, and several of its details conflicted with State Department originals.
